skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Increased the number of validated demand signals from 9 to 12 across requirement descriptions and evidence fields.
- Updated documentation in SKILL.md, README.md, and localized files to reflect the broader demand.
- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.
- No functional or workflow changes; this version clarifies and expands evidence of need.

llm.summary: This text-only skill does not show theft or destructive behavior, but its automatic activation triggers are too broad and could steer unrelated chats.

dimensions.detail: No artifact requests credential access, local profile/session stores, broad indexing, network calls beyond reference links, shell execution, or external tool authority.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The OpenAI agent metadata enables implicit invocation, so the broad trigger language can cause automatic use without an explicit user request for this named skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks to trigger on very common terms such as security, gate, every, must, pass, before, activate, and bug fix, which is broader than the stated SkillScan-style workflow purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, credential handling, or automatic mutation path was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a workflow helper for SkillScan-style security and productivity tasks, and the artifacts only contain markdown/yaml instructions, checklists, and planning guidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing in environments with many skills or sensitive workflows. The content is text-only and shows no exfiltration or destructive behavior, but the publisher should narrow activation to explicit SkillScan-style workflow requests or disable implicit invocation.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The overbroad activation concern is supported by the artifacts: SKILL.md, README files, the requirement plan, and agents/openai.yaml all use broad triggers, and implicit invocation is enabled.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language file is a disclosed localized counterpart to English SKILL and README files, so this is a usability note rather than an independent security concern.
